text: Agile methodology is a popular approach in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short cycles called sprints, which usually last two weeks. Each sprint aims to produce a working part of the product. The team holds daily standups, brief morning meetings where members share updates and obstacles. Work is managed through a backlog, a list of tasks and features to complete. These are described as user stories—simple explanations of a feature from a user's perspective. Through iterative development, the product improves gradually after each sprint, allowing teams to adapt quickly to changes and customer feedback.
